fundamental.headline: Solid business, fairly priced

fundamental.price_text: You're paying about its usual price: its price vs sales is in the middle of its 5-year range. However, it looks pricier than similar companies once growth is considered.

attention.text: Attention: Wikipedia page views 4.4k on 2026-11-06, 0.8× its 30-day normal (5.7k/day) · Hacker News: 1 story in the last 24h (normal 5.9/day), tone of the last week negative.

deeper.title: What the price assumes
deeper.text: The price assumes about 23% a year growth in free cash flow for 10 years, then 3% (discount rate 9.8% = 10-year Treasury 4.8% + 5%; base: last 12 months of free cash flow). For comparison, sales grew 18% last year; 17%/yr over 3 years — roughly in line with its recent growth.

deeper.title: Return on capital
deeper.text: 30% (3 years ago 51%, falling) — each $100 invested in the business (debt + equity, net of cash) earns about $30 a year after tax; return on shareholders' equity 30% (3 years ago 35%).

deeper.title: Signed future revenue
deeper.text: Signed but not yet delivered (remaining performance obligations): $683.0B, up 72% from a year ago — about 2.0× the last 12 months of sales; customer prepayments not yet earned (deferred revenue): $69.6B, up 13% from a year ago.

deeper.title: Multi-year view
deeper.text: Sales grew 17%/yr over 3 years and 14%/yr over 5 years; operating margin today 47% vs a 5-year range of 41–47% (median 45%): near the top of a fairly narrow range.
deeper.margin_position: near the top of a fairly narrow range

deeper.title: Cash returned to shareholders
deeper.text: Returned $48.0B to shareholders over the last 12 months ($21.0B buybacks + $27.0B dividends) = 1.2% of the company's market value. Share count down 0.3% from a year ago (about flat).

deeper.title: Analyst estimates
deeper.text: Next year's earnings-per-share estimate $24.20, up 3% in 90 days (up 2% in the last 30); 24 analysts raised, 4 cut in 30 days. This year's earnings-per-share estimate $20.01, up 2% in 90 days (up 1% in the last 30); 23 analysts raised, 3 cut in 30 days. Source: Yahoo (unofficial).

deeper.title: Vs peers
deeper.text: Compared with 7 peers (ORCL, GOOGL, AMZN, CRM, ADBE, NOW, IBM): sales growth 18% vs a median of 15%; operating margin 47% vs 26%; price/sales 11.4× vs 4.0×.

deeper.title: Where sales come from
deeper.text: By segment, latest quarter vs a year earlier: Agents and infra 83% of sales, up 25%; Devices and consumer 17% of sales, down 3%. Source: 10-Q XBRL.

deeper.title: Insider trading
deeper.text: Last 90 days: no open-market purchases; sales $68.1M, 100% under pre-set 10b5-1 trading plans. Source: SEC Form 4.

deeper.title: New risk factors
deeper.text: 4 new risk-factor headings vs last year's annual report, e.g. “Our cloud and AI strategy requires substantial investments and depends on evolving customer demand, technologi…”; “Our success depends on our ability to develop, deliver, and maintain competitive cloud-based and AI products a…”.

tiles.title: Earnings per share
tiles.sub: +18% vs a year ago · $19.16 over 12 months (GAAP)
tiles.read: Profit per share grew 18%, in step with sales (19%): growth comes from more business, not cost cuts.
tiles.explain: EPS = profit divided by the number of shares. The quarterly figures are the 'adjusted' EPS analysts track (Yahoo); the 12-month figure is the official GAAP number from SEC filings.

tiles.title: Earnings vs forecasts
tiles.sub: last 8 reports · bars = EPS beat (+) or miss (−) vs the average forecast
tiles.read: Beat forecasts 8 quarters running by about 6%, yet the stock fell after 5 of them: beats are already expected.
tiles.explain: A 'beat' means reported EPS came in above the average analyst forecast. Source: Yahoo (unofficial).

tiles.title: Sales growth
tiles.read: Sales up 19% from a year ago, about as fast as two quarters ago (18%): steady demand.
tiles.explain: Growth of quarterly sales (revenue) compared with the same quarter a year earlier.

tiles.title: Profit margins
tiles.read: Each $100 of sales leaves $47 of operating profit, about the same as a year ago.
tiles.explain: Operating margin = operating profit ÷ sales. Gross margin = what's left after the direct cost of the product.

tiles.title: Free cash flow
tiles.read: Just 42% of reported profit became spare cash: much of the profit is tied up in spending or working capital.
tiles.explain: Free cash flow = cash from operations minus spending on equipment and buildings: money the company could return or reinvest.

tiles.title: Price vs profits (P/E)
tiles.read: You pay 28× last year's profit (lower than 70% of the last 5 years; above peers' 19).
tiles.explain: P/E = share price ÷ earnings per share. Forward P/E uses next year's forecast earnings.

tiles.title: Next earnings
tiles.read: Reports Jan 27; analysts expect EPS of $4.86, up 17% from a year ago. It usually moves about 6% the day after, so expect a swing.
tiles.explain: Consensus = the average analyst forecast (Yahoo, unofficial). The typical move is the average size of the stock's next-day move after its last reports, not an options-implied figure.

tiles.title: Company outlook
tiles.read: No numeric outlook was found in the latest earnings release, so the next report carries more surprise risk.
tiles.explain: Guidance = what management says it expects for the next quarter or year, from its 8-K earnings release.

tiles.title: Forecast changes
tiles.read: Next year's EPS forecast is up 3% in 90 days (24 raised, 4 cut lately): forecasts are edging up.
tiles.explain: How the average analyst forecast for next year's earnings per share changed (Yahoo, unofficial).
